compiled_state.title: As a CI reviewer pipeline, I load the same agent prompt files as local /dso:review
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Replace dispatch.py's hardcoded 5-line _SYSTEM_PROMPT with logic that loads code-reviewer-{light,standard,deep-arch,deep-correctness,deep-verification,deep-hygiene,security-red-team,security-blue-team,performance,test-quality}.md from disk and injects each as the litellm.completion() system prompt for its tier
**Why**: CI parity (SC2): same prompts via litellm. Closes the local-passes-CI-fails class of cycles caused by CI's weaker prompt.
**Scope**:
  IN:
  - dispatch.py loads the 10 reviewer agent .md files from plugins/dso/agents/
  - Hardcoded _SYSTEM_PROMPT removed; tier-to-agent mapping respects the same routing local /dso:review uses
  - Schema validation runs on CI reviewer outputs identically to local (write-reviewer-findings.sh equivalent)
  OUT:
  - Two-call architecture wiring (covered by S8)
  - Overlay parallel dispatch (S3)
  - classifier.sh CI bootstrap (S2)
  - Deep-arch synthesis approximation (S4)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, CI llm-review runs use the same code-reviewer-*.md agent files as /dso:review and produce findings under the same schema and rubric
  ← Satisfies: "Single source of truth for review prompts (CI parity)"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Testing] Smoke test CI step verifies dispatch.py can load all 10 agent files; missing file fails fast
- [Maintainability] Loader path uses CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT env var (set in ci.yml per S2)

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
